statement: When a unit's rights status changes to withdrawn — consent revoked, licence expired, or an equivalent event — every artefact whose training manifest cites that unit is identified via the registry (a query, per RBM-20's design, not a search) and is either re-derived without the unit or recalled. Re-derivation trains a replacement artefact excluding the withdrawn unit, using the same run configuration recorded in the original training manifest, and passes it through DAP-31 and MOAC as a new artefact before it replaces the original in the registry. Recall withdraws the original artefact's registry entry and, where the artefact was already delivered under DAP-10, notifies the receiving party that the artefact's rights basis has changed. A unit's contribution to the estate release budget (DAP-35) is NOT refunded on unlearning — the privacy loss from the original release already occurred; unlearning restores the artefact's cleanliness going forward, not the budget already spent.
intended_outcome: DAP-38 is demonstrably enforced as written, with authority-compatible behavior and refusal/record traces.

statement: A registered artefact MUST be served semantics-stable: identical input, identical seed, identical sampling parameters produce identical output from the identical registered artefact, regardless of memory placement, hardware tier, concurrent load, or storage medium. Resource pressure MAY reduce speed — time-to-first-token, tokens per second — and MUST NOT alter precision, truncate context, substitute a different artefact, or change routing semantics. A serving path that cannot uphold this refuses to serve rather than serving a semantically different model. Verification at load: the serving stack verifies the artefact's hash against the register before the first token. Verification in operation: a token-exact reproduction check against a reference path is runnable on demand and on a standing schedule (cadence: ruled, R-13). A merged-adapter checkpoint is a distinct artefact with its own hash and its own register entry — it passes the gates as itself, on DAP-37's own new-hash precedent.
intended_outcome: A20.15 is demonstrably enforced as written, with authority-compatible behavior and refusal/record traces.

statement: Every verdict Grey Mirror passes to Mkono MUST carry a certificate: the set of observed data points that satisfy a ratified certificate requirement (A5.20) for the behaviour asserted, with the requirement's ID and references to the observation records. A certificate contains evidence only. It MUST NOT contain a confidence, score, strength, or probability, and the verdict schema has no field for one — enforced by a signature-as-guard test on CP-S2's precedent. A verdict carrying no certificate is a foundation verdict: it MAY unlock only the reversible ladder — annotate, shape, contain — and severance remains reachable solely from A5.2's registry, unchanged. Mkono's action on a certified verdict is evidenced by that certificate, written to the Ledger with the action. A certificate is legible by construction: it states what was seen, never how worried the detector was.
intended_outcome: A5.19 is demonstrably enforced as written, with authority-compatible behavior and refusal/record traces.

statement: Every unsure case — a verdict with no applicable requirement, or an action routed under AC-4 — enters the research queue with its full observation record. A human ratifies through RBM-8. The output is a new or amended certificate requirement, or a ratified benign pattern so identical conduct is not re-queued. Research runs outside the hot path; the live case receives graduated response meanwhile, exactly as before.

statement: | Assertion Floor | Subjects: any principal requesting a composed answer. Objects: the claim being composed. Operations: assert, compose, refuse. Rule: no sentence enters a composed answer without a per-sentence anchor to material; an unanchorable sentence is refused, not weakened (Doc 4 A2, A5.5). | | **SFP-2** | Certainty-to-Evidence Binding | Subjects: the Watch's response function (Mkono). Objects: severance authority. Operations: unlock, withhold. Rule: severance unlocks only from the closed six-signal registry; no confidence score, however high, is an eligible input (Doc 3 A5.2). | | **SFP-3** | Acceptance Floor | Subjects: any training run. Objects: model output. Operations: accept, refuse. Rule: every stated criterion satisfied or the run is refused in full; no partial acceptance (Promise #22, MOAC). | | **SFP-4** | Custody Floor | Subjects: any data crossing the chokepoint. Objects: the crossing itself. Operations: cross, de-identify, re-identify. Rule: no asset crosses without de-identification appropriate to its custody class (Promise #1, A5.1–A5.3). | | **SFP-5** | Non-Conformance Ceiling | Subjects: any actor whose behavioural signature drifts from its declared conduct. Objects: the actor's trust discount. Operations: reduce, revoke. Rule: loss of conformance alone returns an actor to baseline verification; it is never, by itself, grounds for conviction (Doc 3 A5.7). | | **SFP-6** | Release Budget | Subjects: all external parties, jointly and severally. Objects: the estate's total information release. Operations: release, refuse. Rule: total release across all parties, operations, and time is bounded; exceeding it is a floor violation, not a negotiable ceiling (DAP-35). | | **SFP-7** | Reproduction Ceiling | Subjects: any artefact or output leaving a component boundary. Objects: controlled-unit content. Operations: egress, refuse. Rule: no artefact or output passes carrying reproduction of a controlled unit above the ruled threshold (DAP-31, A5.15). |
intended_outcome: SFP-1 is demonstrably enforced as written, with authority-compatible behavior and refusal/record traces.
